class_declaration.note: name from childForFieldName('name'); extends base may be identifier OR member_expression (qualified heritage)

method_definition.note: constructor -> Constructor kind; get/set -> Property kind; # members strip prefix and mark private

field_definition.note: # private fields stripped to clean name, metadata.isPrivate

variable_declarator.note: module-scope only; require() bindings are imports never symbols; locals/params/lambda params NEVER symbols

assignment_expression.note: module.exports / exports.x chains -> exports; X.prototype.m = fn -> method symbol

import_statement.note: ES6 imports; items from import_clause (default / named_imports / namespace_import); alias is the local binding

new_expression.note: constructor identifier or member_expression property; JS_GLOBAL_CONSTRUCTORS filtered

call_expression.note: member calls -> property target; require() -> imports edge; dynamic import() is gap J2

instanceof_check.note: binary_expression with instanceof operator; right operand is the checked type (JS's only unambiguous named-type usage)

member_expression.note: root-anchored Uses at 0.6; call-callee double-emission is gap J4

expressions_requiring_uses_or_calls: template_substitution (gap J3: `${x}` emits no Uses on x)
_notes: Family contract: 1 + decision points; short-circuit operators count; else never adds.
JS has NO type system — the only named-type usage is instanceof (references).
JSX is native to the javascript grammar (8 types) — unlike TS where it lives in the tsx dialect.
